renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: ascat_profile
  title: Allele-specific copy-number profile
  description: |-
    Each line is a called copy-number segment: its total copy number as a log2 ratio against two copies on the upper panel, and its expected B-allele frequency on the lower one. It answers where the tumour genome gains, loses or keeps its copy number, and where one allele is lost.
    How to read: segments above the upper dotted line are gains and those below the lower one are losses. A BAF far from 0.5 at an unchanged copy number is copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity, which the total copy number alone never shows. Zoom on a chromosome to read the allele-specific counts in the label.
    Lines and annotations: the dotted lines at log2 0.322 and -0.415 are log2(2.5/2) and log2(1.5/2), the total copy numbers of 2.5 and 1.5 where a rounded call leaves two. They are an arithmetic reference defined by this catalog, not an ASCAT cut-off. The dotted line at BAF 0.5 is the balanced state.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20837533/
  kind: cnv_profile
  config:
    gain_threshold: 0.322
    loss_threshold: -0.415
  roles:
    sample: sample
    chrom: chrom
    start: start
    end: end
    log2: log2
    baf: baf
    copy_number: copy_number
    segment: segment
    label: label

- component: card
  id: ascat_cn_spread
  title: Copy number spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median total copy number over the called segments, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers whether the tumour genome sits near the diploid baseline or is shifted.
    How to read: a median of two with a short box means a mostly balanced genome. A higher median or a long box points to widespread gains or a whole-genome duplication. Segments differ in length, so open the profile to see how much of the genome each level covers.
  column: copy_number
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Copy-number segments
  description: |-
    Each row is a called segment with its position, total copy number, expected B-allele frequency and allele-specific label. It answers the exact boundaries and allele counts behind the profile.
    How to read: sort by copy number to list gains and losses, or look for rows with a BAF away from 0.5 and a copy number of two, which are copy-neutral LOH.
  columns:
  - sample
  - chrom
  - start
  - end
  - copy_number
  - baf
  - label

- component: card
  id: ascat_purity_card
  title: Tumour purity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of sequenced cells that carry the tumour genome (ASCAT's aberrant cell fraction), and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how clean the tumour content is.
    How to read: values near one mean a nearly pure tumour sample. Low purity flattens the copy-number profile and makes calls less certain, so treat the profiles of the lowest samples with care.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20837533/
  column: purity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: ascat_ploidy_card
  title: Tumour ploidy
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median average copy number of the tumour genome, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers whether the tumours are near diploid or aneuploid.
    How to read: a value near two means a near-diploid genome and values well above it point to whole-genome duplication. A fit that jumps to an odd ploidy with low purity can be wrong, so check the profile of that sample.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20837533/
  column: ploidy
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  id: ascat_fit_table
  title: Purity and ploidy per sample
  description: |-
    Each row is a tumour sample with ASCAT's fitted purity and ploidy. It answers the exact fit behind each copy-number profile.
    How to read: read purity and ploidy together, since a low purity with an unusual ploidy is the usual sign of an ambiguous fit.
  columns:
  - sample
  - purity
  - ploidy
